caseStudies.subtitle: CASE STUDY 01
caseStudies.title: Scaling PLG → SLG at an AI Video Platform
caseStudies.challenge: Product-led AI company hitting inflection point needed to build enterprise GTM from scratch — new personas, new sales motion, new marketing stack — while maintaining PLG momentum.
caseStudies.approach: Built the full marketing function: messaging architecture, persona framework, enterprise sales enablement, pricing strategy, community-led growth, and a RevOps stack connecting 15+ systems.
caseStudies.outcomes: Path to $20M+ in enterprise revenue. Aligned org around Active Seats as Tier 1 KPI. Built 78K+ member community. Launched SEO localization across 15 languages and 5 regions.

caseStudies.subtitle: CASE STUDY 02
caseStudies.title: Competitive Positioning for a DevSecOps Platform
caseStudies.challenge: Developer security platform competing against 10x larger incumbents needed differentiated positioning, a POV-based sales process, and content that resonated with technical buyers.
caseStudies.approach: Built competitive comparison pages with data-driven messaging. Created POV templates and success criteria frameworks for enterprise deals. Developed battlecards and enablement programs.
caseStudies.outcomes: Comparison pages became top converting assets. POV win rates increased through structured evaluation criteria. Sales confidence improved via systematic enablement program.

caseStudies.subtitle: CASE STUDY 03
caseStudies.title: Underdog Marketing for an Enterprise Content Platform
caseStudies.challenge: Enterprise content governance platform competing against household-name cloud storage giants (think: 50x brand awareness gap) needed to win on differentiation, not budget.
caseStudies.approach: Led product tour experiences, interactive demos, and content that reframed the category around compliance and governance — where incumbents were weakest. Built integrated campaigns spanning SEO, events, and customer advocacy.
caseStudies.outcomes: Product tours became primary conversion driver. Repositioned brand from 'file sharing' to 'content governance' — a defensible category. Analyst recognition followed.
